mechanism_narrative: A sustained quarterly expansion in real GDP (GDPC1) above 2.0% year-over-year signals strengthening economic fundamentals that directly boost corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: GDPC1 growth above 2.0% YoY correlates with negative 20-day forward returns in more than 50% of cases, or Rank IC falls below 0.04 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) declines below 0.20% for three consecutive months, it triggers aggressive monetary easing that reduces discount rates for equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS below 0.20% for 3 months yields negative 5-day returns in >50% of instances, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over 2-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 7.0% and rise in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 150,000 jobs signals a tightening labor market that increases consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: UNRATE < 7.0% and PAYEMS > 150k fails to predict positive returns: 60-day returns negative in >50% of cases, or interaction term p-value >0.05.

mechanism_narrative: During industrial production contractions (INDPRO < 95.0 index), manufacturing output declines signal reduced corporate capacity utilization and earnings pressure, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 95.0 correlates with positive 20-day returns in >50% of cases, or Rank IC exceeds -0.04 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% YoY) triggers expectations of aggressive monetary policy tightening, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL > 3.0% YoY yields positive 60-day returns in >50% of periods, or Rank IC > -0.05 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate (UNRATE) rise above 7.5% for two consecutive months indicates labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE > 7.5% for 2 months yields positive 5-day returns in >50% of cases, or Rank IC > -0.03 over 2-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent growth in housing starts (HOUST > 1000k units) and retail sales (RSAFS > 400,000 million dollars) signals robust consumer demand that accelerates corporate revenue growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: HOUST > 1000k and RSAFS > 400k fails to predict positive returns: 20-day returns negative in >50% of cases, or interaction term p-value >0.05.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%), higher interest rates reduce corporate leverage and equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 4.0% correlates with positive 60-day returns in >50% of periods, or Rank IC > -0.04 over 3-year rolling windows.
